}\n397\t\n398\t        Some(j * grid.nx as usize + i)\n399\t    }\n400\t}\n401\t\n402\t/// Parameters unique to GDT 3.40 (Gaussian Latitude/Longitude).\n403\t///\n404\t/// A Gaussian grid has **uniform longitude** spacing but **non-uniform latitude**\n405\t/// spacing — the latitudes are the zeros of the associated Legendre polynomial\n406\t/// P_N(sin φ) between the equator and the pole. Template-specific projection parameters (Lambert, polar stereo, …).\n606\t    pub projection: GridProjection,\n607\t}\n608\t\n609\timpl GridDefinition {\n610\t    /// True if points are stored with i (longitude) varying fastest (row-major).\n611\t    pub fn i_positive(&self) -> bool {\n612\t        self.scanning_mode & 0x80 == 0\n613\t    }\n614\t\n615\t    /// True if j (latitude) increases from (boustrophedon).\n621\t    pub fn alternating_rows(&self) -> bool {\n622\t        self.scanning_mode & 0x20 != 0\n623\t    }\n624\t}\n625\t\n626\t// ── Grid values (Section 6 + 7) ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n627\t\n628\t/// Decoded grid: either all present (Dense) or with a missing-value mask.\n629\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n630\tpub enum GridValues {\n631\t    /// All points present; length == grid.num_data_points.\n632\t    Dense(Vec<f64>),\n633\t    /// `values[i]` is meaningful only when `present[i]` is true.\n634\t    Masked { values: Vec<f64>, present: Vec<bool> },\n635\t}\n636\t\n637\timpl GridValues {\n638\t    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n639\t        match self {\n640\t            GridValues::Dense(v) => v.len(),\n641\t            GridValues::Masked { values, .. } => values.len(),\n642\t        }\n643\t    }\n644\t\n645\t    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n646\t        self.len() == 0\n647\t    }\n648\t\n649\t    /// Iterate over (value, is_present) pairs.\n650\t    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (f64, bool)> + '_ {\n651\t        match self {\n652\t            GridValues::Dense(v) => {\n653\t                let v2: Vec<bool> = vec![true; v.len()];\n654\t                v.iter()\n655\t                    .zip(v2)\n656\t                    .map(|(&val, p)| (val, p))\n657\t                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n658\t                    .into_iter()\n659\t            }\n660\t            GridValues::Masked { values, present } => values\n661\t                .iter()\n662\t                .zip(present.iter())\n663\t                .map(|(&val, &p)| (val, p))\n664\t                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n665\t                .into_iter(),\n666\t        }\n667\t    }\n668\t\n669\t    /// Value at a flat index; None if the point is masked, absent, or out of bounds.\n670\t    pub fn get_at(&self, idx: usize) -> Option<f64> {\n671\t        match self {\n672\t            GridValues::Dense(v) => v.get(idx).copied(),\n673\t            GridValues::Masked { values, present } => {\n674\t                if *present.get(idx)? { values.get(idx).copied() } else { None }\n675\t            }\n676\t        }\n677\t    }\n678\t\n679\t    /// Bilinear interpolation from four corners produced by [`GridDefinition::bilinear_corners`].\n680\t    /// Returns None if any corner is masked or out of bounds.\n681\t    pub fn bilinear(&self, c: &BilinearCorners) -> Option<f64> {\n682\t        let v_nw = self.get_at(c.idx_nw)?;\n683\t        let v_ne = self.get_at(c.idx_ne)?;\n684\t        let v_sw = self.get_at(c.idx_sw)?;\n685\t        let v_se = self.get_at(c.idx_se)?;\n686\t        Some(\n687\t            (1.0 - c.fx) * (1.0 - c.fy) * v_nw\n688\t                + c.fx * (1.0 - c.fy) * v_ne\n689\t                + (1.0 - c.fx) * c.fy * v_sw\n690\t                + c.fx * c.fy * v_se,\n691\t        )\n692\t    }\n693\t}\n694\t\n695\t// ── Grid point extraction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n696\t\n697\t/// Four corner indices and fractional weights for bilinear interpolation.\n698\t/// Produced by [`GridDefinition::bilinear_corners`].\n699\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\n700\tpub struct BilinearCorners {\n701\t    /// Flat index of the \"north-west\" corner (lower j, lower i).\n702\t    pub    pub idx_sw: usize,\n707\t    /// Flat index of the \"south-east\" corner (higher j, higher i).\n708\t    pub idx_se: usize,\n709\t    /// Fractional longitude within the cell [0, 1].\n710\t    pub index.\n717\t    ///\n718\t    /// Dispatches on `self.projection`:\n719\t    /// - [`GridProjection::LatLon`]: regular lat/lon arithmetic (template 0).\n720\t    ///   Returns `None` if increments are zero or the query is outside the grid.\n721\t    /// - [`GridProjection::RotatedLatLon`]: rotated lat/lon grid.\n722\t    ///   Rotates the query point into the rotated coordinate system, then\n723\t    ///   applies regular lat/lon arithmetic.\n724\t    /// - [`GridProjection::PolarStereographic`]: polar stereographic projection.\n725\t    ///   Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n726\t    /// - [`GridProjection::LambertConformal`]: Lambert conformal conic projection.\n727\t    ///   Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n728\t    /// - [`GridProjection::GaussianLatLon`]: Gaussian lat/lon grid.\n729\t    ///   Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n730\t    pub fn nearest_index(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n731\t        match &self.projection {\n732\t            GridProjection::LatLon => self.nearest_index_latlon(lat, lon),\n733\t            GridProjection::RotatedLatLon(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n734\t            GridProjection::PolarStereographic(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n735\t            GridProjection::LambertConformal(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n736\t            GridProjection::GaussianLatLon(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n737\t        }\n738\t    }\n739\t\n740\t    /// Nearest-index for regular lat/lon grids (template 0).\n741\t    fn nearest_index_latlon(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n742\t        if self.di == 0.0 || self.dj == 0.0 {\n743\t            return None;\n744\t        }\n745\t        let mut fi = Self::lon_to_fi(lon, self.lon_first, self.di, self.nx);\n746\t        // Try ±360° wrap once if out of the [-0.5, nx-0.5] window\n747\t        let nx_f = self.nx as f64;\n748\t        if fi < -0.5 { fi += 360.0 / self.di; }\n749\t        else if fi > nx_f - 0.5 { fi -= 360.0 / self.di; }\n750\t        if fi < -0.5 || fi > nx_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n751\t\n752\t        let fj = self.lat_to_fj(lat);\n753\t        let ny_f = self.ny as f64;\n754\t        if fj < -0.5 || fj > ny_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n755\t\n756\t        let i = fi.round() as usize;\n757\t        let j = fj.round() as usize;\n758\t        Some(j * self.nx as usize + i)\n759\t    }\n760\t\n761\t    /// Bilinear interpolation corners.\n762\t    ///\n763\t    /// Currently implemented for     if !matches!(self.projection, GridProjection::LatLon)\n767\t            || self.di == 0.0\n768\t            || self.dj == 0.0\n769\t        {\n770\t            return None;\n771\t        }\n772\t       if lon_n < 0.0 { lon_n += 360.0; }\n800\t        (lon_n - lon_first) / di\n801\t    }\n802\t\n803\t    /// Fractional row index for a latitude query.\n804\t    fn lat_to_fj(&self, lat: f64) -> }\n811\t}\n812\t\n813\t// ── Field ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n814\t\n815\t/// A single decoded GRIB2 field — the unit of comparison in the differential projection on a sphere.\n    ///\n    /// Returns (x, y) in metres, relative to the projection origin placed at\n    /// (LaD, LoV).  x increases in the +i direction (eastward for north-pole\n    /// projection); y increases in the +j direction (northward).\n    pub fn project_xy(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> (f64, f64) {\n        use std::f64::consts::{FRAC_PI_4, PI};\n        let to_rad = PI / 180.0;\n\n        let phi1 = self.latin1 * to_rad;\n        let phi2 = self.latin2 * to_rad;\n        let phi0 = self.lad * to_rad;\n        let lam0 = self.lov * to_rad;\n        let phi = lat * to_rad;\n\n        // Normalise longitude to within ±π of the central meridian.\n        let mut lam = lon * to_rad;\n        while lam - lam0 > PI { lam -= 2.0 * PI; }\n        while lam0 - lam > PI { lam += 2.0 * PI; }\n\n        let r = Self::EARTH_R;\n\n        // Cone constant n.\n        let n = if (phi1 - phi2).abs() < 1e-8 {\n            phi1.sin()\n        } else {\n            let t1 = (FRAC_PI_4 + phi1 / 2.0).tan();\n            let t2 = (FRAC_PI_4 + phi2 / 2.0).tan();\n            (phi1.cos().ln() - phi2.cos().ln()) / (t2.ln() - t1.ln())\n        };\n\n        // Scale factor F (includes R).\n        let t1 = (FRAC_PI_4 + phi1 / 2.0).tan();\n        let big_f = r * phi1.cos() * t1.powf(n) / n;\n\n        // ρ at reference latitude LaD (defines the y-origin of the local big_f / t.powf(n);\n\n        let theta = n * (lam - lam0);\n        let x = rho * theta.sin();\n        let y = rho0 - rho * theta.cos();\n        (x, y)\n    }\n\n    /// Nearest grid-point flat index for a Lambert conformal grid.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if the query falls outside the grid extent.\n    pub fn nearest_index(&self, grid: &GridDefinition, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n        let (x1, y1) = self.project_xy(grid.lat_first, grid.lon_first);\n        let (xq, yq) = self.project_xy(lat, lon);\n\n        // i increases in the +x direction; j direction depends on scanning mode.\n        let di_f = (xq - x1) / self.dx_m;\n        let dj_f = if grid.j_positive() {\n            (yq - y1) / self.dy_m\n        } else {\n            (y1 - yq) / self.dy_m\n        };\n\n        // Half-cell tolerance for boundary snapping.\n        if di_f < -0.5 || dj_f < -0.5 { return None; }\n        let nx_f = grid.nx as f64;\n        let ny_f = grid.ny as f64;\n        if di_f > nx_f - 0.5 || dj_f > ny_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        let i = di_f.round() as usize;\n        let j = dj_f.round() as usize;\n        if i >= grid.nx as usize || j >= grid.ny as usize { return None; }\n\n        Some(j * grid.nx as usize + i)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parameters unique to GDT 3.20 (Polar Stereographic).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct PolarStereographicParams {\n    /// Latitude where Dx and Dy are specified (degrees, positive N).\n    pub lad: f64,\n    /// Orientation of the grid / central meridian (degrees, positive E, 0–360).\n    pub lov: f64,\n    /// i-direction (x) increment in metres at LaD.\n    pub dx_m: f64,\n    /// j-direction (y) increment in metres at LaD.\n    pub dy_m: f64,\n    /// Projection centre flag (Table 3.5): bit 7 set = South Pole in plane.\n    pub proj_centre: u8,\n}\n\nimpl PolarStereographicParams {\n    /// Earth radius for GRIB2 shape=6 (WMO standard sphere), in metres.\n    const EARTH_R: f64 = 6_371_229.0;\n\n    /// Forward polar stereographic projection on a sphere.\n    ///\n    /// Returns (x, y) in metres in a Cartesian frame centred at the projection\n    /// pole (North or South according to `proj_centre`).\n    ///\n    /// The projection is scaled so that Dx and Dy are exact distances at\n    /// latitude `lad`.  Convention: x increases in the direction 90° east of\n    /// LoV; y increases toward the pole along the LoV meridian.\n    ///\n    /// For North Polar (bit 7 of `proj_centre` == 0):\n    ///   ρ = R · (1 + sin LaD) · cos φ / (1 + sin φ)\n    ///   x = ρ sin θ,   y = −ρ cos θ    (θ = λ − LoV)\n    ///\n    /// For South Polar (bit 7 of `proj_centre` == 1):\n    ///   ρ = R · (1 − sin LaD) · cos φ / (1 − sin φ)\n    ///   x = ρ sin θ,   y = +ρ cos θ\n    pub fn project_xy(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> (f64, f64) {\n        use std::f64::consts::PI;\n        let to_rad = PI / 180.0;\n\n        let phi    = lat * to_rad;\n        let lam    = lon * to_rad;\n        let lam0   = self.lov * to_rad;\n        let phi_d  = self.lad * to_rad;\n\n        // Normalise longitude difference to (−π, π].\n        let mut theta = lam - lam0;\n        while theta >  PI { theta -= 2.0 * PI; }\n        while theta < -PI { theta += 2.0 * PI; }\n\n        let r = Self::EARTH_R;\n        let north_pole = self.proj_centre & 0x80 == 0;\n\n        let (rho, y) = if north_pole {\n            let rho = r * (1.0 + phi_d.sin()) * phi.cos() / (1.0 + phi.sin());\n            let y   = -rho * theta.cos();\n            (rho, y)\n        } else {\n            // South Polar: phi_d is negative (e.g. −60°), so (1 − sin φ_d) > 1.\n            let rho = r * (1.0 - phi_d.sin()) * phi.cos() / (1.0 - phi.sin());\n            let y   = rho * theta.cos();\n            (rho, y)\n        };\n\n        let x = rho * theta.sin();\n        (x, y)\n    }\n\n    /// Nearest grid-point flat index for a polar stereographic grid.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `None` if the query falls outside the grid extent.\n    pub fn nearest_index(&self, grid: &GridDefinition, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n        let (x0, y0) = self.project_xy(grid.lat_first, grid.lon_first);\n        let (xq, yq) = self.project_xy(lat, lon);\n\n        // i increases in the +x direction; j direction follows scanning mode.\n        let di_f = (xq - x0) / self.dx_m;\n        let dj_f = if grid.j_positive() {\n            (yq - y0) / self.dy_m\n        } else {\n            (y0 - yq) / self.dy_m\n        };\n\n        // Half-cell tolerance for boundary snapping.\n        if di_f < -0.5 || dj_f < -0.5 { return None; }\n        let nx_f = grid.nx as f64;\n        let ny_f = grid.ny as f64;\n        if di_f > nx_f - 0.5 || dj_f > ny_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        let i = di_f.round() as usize;\n        let j = dj_f.round() as usize;\n        if i >= grid.nx as usize || j >= grid.ny as usize { return None; }\n\n        Some(j * grid.nx as usize + i)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parameters unique to GDT 3.40 (Gaussian Latitude/Longitude).\n///\n/// A Gaussian grid has **uniform longitude** spacing but **non-uniform latitude**\n/// spacing — the latitudes are the zeros of the associated Legendre polynomial\n/// P_N(sin φ) between the equator and the pole.  The parameter N is the number\n/// of latitude circles from the pole to the equator; the grid has 2N parallels\n/// (or 2N+1 if the poles are included, depending on the implementation).\n///\n/// For nearest-point queries the latitudes are approximated as linearly spaced\n/// between La1 and La2 (equal to the true Gaussian latitudes at the corners).\n/// True Gaussian quadrature placement would require computing the zeros of\n/// Legendre polynomials — a valid follow-up optimisation once a real fixture\n/// exercises this path.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct GaussianLatLonParams {\n    /// N — number of parallels between the Pole and the Equator.\n    pub n_parallels: u32,\n}\n\n/// Parameters unique to GDT 3.1 (Rotated Latitude/Longitude).\n///\n/// A rotated lat/lon grid uses a rotated coordinate system where the \"pole\"\n/// of the grid is not at the geographic pole. The rotation is defined by\n/// specifying the geographic location of the southern pole of the rotated\n/// system and the rotation angle of the local coordinate system.\n///\n/// Nearest-point queries work by rotating the query point from geographic\n/// coordinates into the rotated coordinate system, then applying the regular\n/// lat/lon arithmetic.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub struct RotatedLatLonParams {\n    /// Latitude of the southern pole of the rotation (degrees, positive N).\n    pub lat_pole_rot: f64,\n    /// Longitude of the southern pole of the rotation (degrees, positive E, 0–360).\n    pub lon_pole_rot: f64,\n    /// Angle of rotation of the local coordinate system (degrees, last 2 digits are fractional).\n    pub angle_rot: f64,\n}\n\nimpl GaussianLatLonParams {\n    /// Nearest-grid-point flat index for a Gaussian lat/lon grid.\n    ///\n    /// Longitude is uniform (Di stored in the common `di` field).\n    /// Latitude is approximated as uniform between La1 and La2\n    /// (Nj steps), which is exact at the corners and a close approximation\n    /// elsewhere.  Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n    pub fn nearest_index(&self, grid: &GridDefinition, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n        if grid.di == 0.0 { return None; }\n        let nj = grid.ny as f64;\n        if nj <= 1.0 { return None; }\n\n        // Longitude: same uniform arithmetic as GDT 3.0.\n        let mut fi = GridDefinition::lon_to_fi(lon, grid.lon_first, grid.di, grid.nx);\n        let nx_f = grid.nx as f64;\n        if fi < -0.5 { fi += 360.0 / grid.di; }\n        else if fi > nx_f - 0.5 { fi -= 360.0 / grid.di; }\n        if fi < -0.5 || fi > nx_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        // Latitude: approximate as uniform between La1 and La2.\n        let dlat = (grid.lat_last - grid.lat_first) / (nj - 1.0);\n        if dlat.abs() < 1e-12 { return None; }\n        let fj = (lat - grid.lat_first) / dlat;\n        if fj < -0.5 || fj > nj - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        let i = fi.round() as usize;\n        let j = fj.round() as usize;\n        if i >= grid.nx as usize || j >= grid.ny as usize { return None; }\n        Some(j * grid.nx as usize + i)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RotatedLatLonParams {\n    /// Rotate a geographic (lat, lon) point into the rotated coordinate system.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the (lat_rot, lon_rot) coordinates in the rotated system.\n    /// The rotation follows the standard GRIB2 rotated pole definition:\n    /// 1. Rotate around the Z axis by -(lon_pole_rot + 180°)\n    /// 2. Rotate around the Y axis by -(lat_pole_rot + 90°)\n    /// 3. Rotate around the Z axis by angle_rot\n    fn geographic_to_rotated(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> (f64, f64) {\n        use std::f64::consts::PI;\n        let to_rad = PI / 180.0;\n        let to_deg = 180.0 / PI;\n\n        let lat_rad = lat * to_rad;\n        let lon_rad = lon * to_rad;\n        let pole_lat_rad = self.lat_pole_rot * to_rad;\n        let pole_lon_rad = self.lon_pole_rot * to_rad;\n        let angle_rad = self.angle_rot * to_rad;\n\n        // Convert to Cartesian coordinates\n        let x = lat_rad.cos() * lon_rad.cos();\n        let y = lat_rad.cos() * lon_rad.sin();\n        let z = lat_rad.sin();\n\n        // Rotate around Z axis by -(pole_lon + 180°)\n        let rot_z1 = -(pole_lon_rad + PI);\n        let x1 = x * rot_z1.cos() - y * rot_z1.sin();\n        let y1 = x * rot_z1.sin() + y * rot_z1.cos();\n        let z1 = z;\n\n        // Rotate around Y axis by -(pole_lat + 90°)\n        let rot_y = -(pole_lat_rad + PI / 2.0);\n        let x2 = x1 * rot_y.cos() + z1 * rot_y.sin();\n        let y2 = y1;\n        let z2 = -x1 * rot_y.sin() + z1 * rot_y.cos();\n\n        // Rotate around Z axis by angle_rot\n        let x3 = x2 * angle_rad.cos() - y2 * angle_rad.sin();\n        let y3 = x2 * angle_rad.sin() + y2 * angle_rad.cos();\n        let z3 = z2;\n\n        // Convert back to spherical coordinates\n        let lat_rot = z3.atan2(y3.hypot(x3)) * to_deg;\n        let lon_rot = y3.atan2(x3) * to_deg;\n        (lat_rot, lon_rot)\n    }\n\n    /// Nearest-grid-point flat index for a rotated lat/lon grid.\n    ///\n    /// Rotates the query point into the rotated coordinate system, then\n    /// applies the same uniform-grid arithmetic as GDT 3.0.\n    /// Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n    pub fn nearest_index(&self, grid: &GridDefinition, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n        if grid.di == 0.0 || grid.dj == 0.0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n\n        // Rotate the query point into the rotated coordinate system\n        let (lat_rot, lon_rot) = self.geographic_to_rotated(lat, lon);\n\n        // Use the same arithmetic as GDT 3.0 in the rotated system\n        let mut fi = GridDefinition::lon_to_fi(lon_rot, grid.lon_first, grid.di, grid.nx);\n        let nx_f = grid.nx as f64;\n        if fi < -0.5 { fi += 360.0 / grid.di; }\n        else if fi > nx_f - 0.5 { fi -= 360.0 / grid.di; }\n        if fi < -0.5 || fi > nx_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        let fj = grid.lat_to_fj(lat_rot);\n        let ny_f = grid.ny as f64;\n        if fj < -0.5 || fj > ny_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        let i = fi.round() as usize;\n        let j = fj.round() as usize;\n        if i >= grid.nx as usize || j >= grid.ny as usize { return None; }\n        Some(j * grid.nx as usize + i)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Template-specific grid projection parameters.\n///\n/// Carried inside [`GridDefinition`] to hold parameters that are only present\n/// for projected (non-lat/lon) grid types. lon_first: f64,\n    /// Latitude of last grid point (0.0 for projected grids).\n    pub lat_last: f64,\n    /// Longitude of last grid point (0.0 for projected grids).\n    pub lon_last: f64,\n    /// i-direction increment in degrees (0 if not uniform or for projected grids).\n    pub di: f64,\n    /// j-direction increment in degrees (0 if not uniform or for projected grids).\n    pub dj: f64,\n    /// Scanning mode flags (Table 3.4): bit 7 = +i direction, bit 6 = +j direction, …\n    pub scanning_mode: u8,\n    /// Resolution and component flags (Table 3.3).\n    pub resolution_flags: u8,\n    /// Shape of the Earth (Table 3.2): 0=spherical 6367.47km, 6=WGS84, …\n    pub shape_of_earth: u8,\n    /// Template-specific projection parameters (Lambert, polar stereo, …).\n    pub projection: GridProjection,\n}\n\nimpl GridDefinition {\n    /// True if points are stored with i (longitude) varying fastest (row-major).\n    pub fn i_positive(&self) -> bool {\n        self.scanning_mode & 0x80 == 0\n    }\n\n    /// True if j (latitude) increases from first to last point.\n    pub fn j_positive(&self) -> bool {\n        self.scanning_mode & 0x40 != 0\n    }\n\n    /// True if adjacent rows alternate scan direction (boustrophedon).\n    pub fn alternating_rows(&self) -> bool {\n        self.scanning_mode & 0x20 != 0\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Grid values (Section 6 + 7) ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Decoded grid: either all present (Dense) or with a missing-value mask.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum GridValues {\n    /// All points present; length == grid.num_data_points.\n    Dense(Vec<f64>),\n    /// `values[i]` is meaningful only when `present[i]` is true.\n    Masked { values: Vec<f64>, present: Vec<bool> },\n}\n\nimpl GridValues {\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        match self {\n            GridValues::Dense(v) => v.len(),\n            GridValues::Masked { values, .. } => values.len(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.len() == 0\n    }\n\n    /// Iterate over (value, is_present) pairs.\n    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (f64, bool)> + '_ {\n        match self {\n            GridValues::Dense(v) => {\n                let v2: Vec<bool> = vec![true; v.len()];\n                v.iter()\n                    .zip(v2)\n                    .map(|(&val, p)| (val, p))\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                    .into_iter()\n            }\n            GridValues::Masked { values, present } => values\n                .iter()\n                .zip(present.iter())\n                .map(|(&val, &p)| (val, p))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .into_iter(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Value at a flat index; None if the point is masked, absent, or out of bounds.\n    pub fn get_at(&self, idx: usize) -> Option<f64> {\n        match self {\n            GridValues::Dense(v) => v.get(idx).copied(),\n            GridValues::Masked { values, present } => {\n                if *present.get(idx)? { values.get(idx).copied() } else { None }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Bilinear interpolation from four corners produced by [`GridDefinition::bilinear_corners`].\n    /// Returns None if any corner is masked or out of bounds.\n    pub fn bilinear(&self, c: &BilinearCorners) -> Option<f64> {\n        let v_nw = self.get_at(c.idx_nw)?;\n        let v_ne = self.get_at(c.idx_ne)?;\n        let v_sw = self.get_at(c.idx_sw)?;\n        let v_se = self.get_at(c.idx_se)?;\n        Some(\n            (1.0 - c.fx) * (1.0 - c.fy) * v_nw\n                + c.fx * (1.0 - c.fy) * v_ne\n                + (1.0 - c.fx) * c.fy * v_sw\n                + c.fx * c.fy * v_se,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Grid point extraction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Four corner indices and fractional weights for bilinear interpolation.\n/// Produced by [`GridDefinition::bilinear_corners`].\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct BilinearCorners {\n    /// Flat index of the \"north-west\" corner (lower j, lower i).\n    pub idx_nw: usize,\n    /// Flat index of the \"north-east\" corner (lower j, higher i).\n    pub idx_ne: usize,\n    /// Flat index of the \"south-west\" corner (higher j, lower i).\n    pub idx_sw: usize,\n    /// Flat index of the \"south-east\" corner (higher j, higher i).\n    pub idx_se: usize,\n    /// Fractional longitude within the cell [0, 1].\n    pub fx: f64,\n    /// Fractional latitude toward the \"south\" edge (increasing j) [0, 1].\n    pub fy: f64,\n}\n\nimpl GridDefinition {\n    /// Nearest-grid-point flat index.\n    ///\n    /// Dispatches on `self.projection`:\n    /// - [`GridProjection::LatLon`]: regular lat/lon arithmetic (template 0).\n    ///   Returns `None` if increments are zero or the query is outside the grid.\n    /// - [`GridProjection::RotatedLatLon`]: rotated lat/lon grid.\n    ///   Rotates the query point into the rotated coordinate system, then\n    ///   applies regular lat/lon arithmetic.\n    /// - [`GridProjection::PolarStereographic`]: polar stereographic projection.\n    ///   Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n    /// - [`GridProjection::LambertConformal`]: Lambert conformal conic projection.\n    ///   Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n    /// - [`GridProjection::GaussianLatLon`]: Gaussian lat/lon grid.\n    ///   Returns `None` if the query is outside the grid extent.\n    pub fn nearest_index(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n        match &self.projection {\n            GridProjection::LatLon => self.nearest_index_latlon(lat, lon),\n            GridProjection::RotatedLatLon(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n            GridProjection::PolarStereographic(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n            GridProjection::LambertConformal(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n            GridProjection::GaussianLatLon(p) => p.nearest_index(self, lat, lon),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Nearest-index for regular lat/lon grids (template 0).\n    fn nearest_index_latlon(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<usize> {\n        if self.di == 0.0 || self.dj == 0.0 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let mut fi = Self::lon_to_fi(lon, self.lon_first, self.di, self.nx);\n        // Try ±360° wrap once if out of the [-0.5, nx-0.5] window\n        let nx_f = self.nx as f64;\n        if fi < -0.5 { fi += 360.0 / self.di; }\n        else if fi > nx_f - 0.5 { fi -= 360.0 / self.di; }\n        if fi < -0.5 || fi > nx_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        let fj = self.lat_to_fj(lat);\n        let ny_f = self.ny as f64;\n        if fj < -0.5 || fj > ny_f - 0.5 { return None; }\n\n        let i = fi.round() as usize;\n        let j = fj.round() as usize;\n        Some(j * self.nx as usize + i)\n    }\n\n    /// Bilinear interpolation corners.\n    ///\n    /// Currently implemented for lat/lon grids only.  Returns `None` for\n    /// projected grids, zero-increment grids, or queries outside the grid.\n    pub fn bilinear_corners(&self, lat: f64, lon: f64) -> Option<BilinearCorners> {\n        if !matches!(self.projection, GridProjection::LatLon)\n            || self.di == 0.0\n            || self.dj == 0.0\n        {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let mut fi = Self::lon_to_fi(lon, self.lon_first, self.di, self.nx);\n        let nx1 = (self.nx - 1) as f64;\n        if fi < 0.0 { fi += 360.0 / self.di; }\n        else if fi >= nx1 + 1.0 { fi -= 360.0 / self.di; }\n        if fi < 0.0 || fi >= nx1 { return None; }\n\n        let fj = self.lat_to_fj(lat);\n        let ny1 = (self.ny - 1) as f64;\n        if fj < 0.0 || fj >= ny1 { return None; }\n\n        let i0 = fi.floor() as usize;\n        let j0 = fj.floor() as usize;\n        let nx = self.nx as usize;\n        Some(BilinearCorners {\n            idx_nw: j0 * nx + i0,\n            idx_ne: j0 * nx + (i0 + 1),\n            idx_sw: (j0 + 1) * nx + i0,\n            idx_se: (j0 + 1) * nx + (i0 + 1),\n            fx: fi - i0 as f64,\n            fy: fj - j0 as f64,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Fractional column index for a longitude query.\n    fn lon_to_fi(lon: f64, lon_first: f64, di: f64, _nx: u32) -> f64 {\n        // Normalize to [0, 360) to match GRIB2 convention, then compute offset\n        let mut lon_n = lon % 360.0;\n        if lon_n < 0.0 { lon_n += 360.0; }\n        (lon_n - lon_first) / di\n    }\n\n    /// Fractional row index for a latitude query.\n    fn lat_to_fj(&self, lat: f64) -> f64 {\n        if self.j_positive() {\n            (lat - self.lat_first) / self.dj\n        } else {\n            (self.lat_first - lat) / self.dj\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ── Field ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A single decoded GRIB2 field — the unit of comparison in the differential harness.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Field {\n    // ── Identification (Section 1) ───────────────────────────────────────\n    /// Originating center (Table 0): 7=US-NCEP, 98=ECMWF, …\n    pub center: u16,\n    pub subcenter: u16,\n\n    // ── Parameter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    pub parameter: ParameterId,\n\n    // ── Forecast ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    pub forecast: ForecastTime,\n\n    // ── Level ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    pub level: Level,\n\n    // ── Ensemble (absent for deterministic products) ─────────────────────\n    pub ensemble: Option<Ensemble>,\n\n    // ── Grid geometry ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    pub grid: GridDefinition,\n\n    // ── Decoded values ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    pub values: GridValues,\n\n    // ── Template numbers (for coverage tracking) ─────────────────────────\n    /// Grid Definition Template (3.x).\n    pub gdt_template: u16,\n    /// Product Definition Template (4.x).\n    pub pdt_template: u16,\n    /// Data Representation Template (5.x).\n    pub drt_template: u16,\n\n    // ── Packing metadata (tolerance derivation) ───────────────────────────\n    pub packing: PackingInfo,\n}\n\n// ── Lazy field ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A GRIB2 field with Section 7 data stored as raw bytes — not yet decoded.\n///\n/// Used by the lazy point-extraction path.  The caller extracts individual\n/// grid points on demand:\n/// - DRT=0 (simple packing) without a bitmap: use [`decode_point_drt0`].\n/// - DRT=2/3 (complex packing, with or without spatial differencing) without a\n///   bitmap: use `decode_all_drt3`; the full grid must be decoded because DRT=3\n///   spatial differencing prevents true random access.  `complex_extra` carries\n///   the Section 5 group-structure parameters needed by that decoder.\n///\n/// For other templates or fields with a bitmap, `section7_raw` is empty and\n/// the lazy path returns `None`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct LazyField {\n    pub center: u16,\n    pub subcenter: u16,\n    pub parameter: ParameterId,\n    pub forecast: ForecastTime,\n    pub level: Level,\n    pub ensemble: Option<Ensemble>,\n    pub grid: GridDefinition,\n    pub packing: PackingInfo,\n    pub gdt_template: u16,\n    pub pdt_template: u16,\n    pub drt_template: u16,\n    /// Raw Section 7 body bytes.\n    ///\n    /// Non-empty for DRT=0, DRT=2, and DRT=3 fields without a bitmap.\n    /// Empty for all other templates or when a bitmap is present.\n    pub section7_raw: Vec<u8>,\n    /// True when the message has an active bitmap (lazy extraction unsupported).\n    pub has_bitmap: bool,\n    /// Group-structure parameters from Section 5; populated for DRT=2/3 fields.\n    ///\n    /// Required to call `decode_all_drt3`.  `None` for DRT=0, DRT=40, DRT=41,\n    /// and bitmap fields.\n    pub complex_extra: Option<ComplexExtra>,\n}\n\n// ── Message ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A GRIB2 message: zero or more fields sharing a common identification section.\n///\n/// A single `.grib2` file may contain multiple concatenated messages.\n/// Within a message, sections 2–7 may repeat to encode multiple fields.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Message {\n    pub fields: Vec<Field>,\n}\n\n// ── Tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reference_time_unix() {\n        let t = ReferenceTime {\n to index 0\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn lambert_nearest_point_offset() {\n        // Projecting la1 + ~1 grid step northward and eastward should give (i,j) ≈ (1,1),\n        // i.e. flat index 1*10 + 1 = 11. pos < 4 {\n208\t            break;\n209\t        }\n210\t        if &bytes[pos..pos + 4] != b\"GRIB\" {\n211\t            return Err(Error::BadMagic(bytes[pos..pos + 4].try_into().unwrap()));\n212\t        }\n213\t\n214\t        let msg_len = decode_message(&bytes[pos..], &mut fields)?;\n215\t        pos += msg_len;\n216\t    }\n217\t\n218\t    Ok(fields)\n219\t}\n220\t\n221\t/// Decode one GRIB2 message (starting at byte 0 of `msg`).\n222\t/// Returns the number of bytes consumed (the total message length).\n223\tfn decode_message(msg: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<Field>) -> Result<usize> {\n224\t    let mut buf = Buf::new(msg);\n225\t\n226\t    // ── Section 0 (Indicator, 16 bytes fixed) ────────────────────────────────\n227\t    // oct 1-4: \"GRIB\"\n228\t    let magic = [buf.read_u8()?, buf.read_u8()?, buf.read_u8()?, buf.read_u8()?];\n229\t    if &magic != b\"GRIB\" {\n230\t        return Err(Error::BadMagic(magic));\n231\t    }\n232\t    buf.skip(2)?; // reserved\n233\t    let discipline = buf.read_u8()?;\n234\t    let edition = buf.read_u8()?;\n235\t    if edition != 2 {\n236\t        return Err(Error::UnknownEdition(edition));\n237\t    }\n238\t    let total_len = buf.read_u64be()? as usize;\n239\t    // Section 0 is now consumed (16 bytes).\n240\t\n241\t    // Validate total length against buffer.\n242\t    if msg.len() < total_len {\n243\t        return Err(Error::TooShort { needed: total_len, got: msg.len() });\n244\t    }\n245\t\n246\t    // ── Section iterator (sections 1-7 + \"7777\") ─────────────────────────────\n247\t    let mut builder = FieldBuilder::default();\n248\t\n249\t    // The message body ends just before the \"7777\" end marker.\n250\t    let body_end = total_len - 4;\n251\t\n252\t    while buf.pos < body_end {\n253\t        // Each section starts with: 4-byte length, 1-byte section number.\n254\t        let sec_start = buf.pos;\n255\t        let sec_len = buf.read_u32be()? as usize;\n256\t        let sec_num = buf.read_u8()?;\n257\t\n258\t        if sec_len < 5 {\n259\t            return Err(Error::TooShort { needed: 5, got: sec_len });\n260\t        }\n261\t        // Remaining bytes in this section (after the 5-byte header).\n262\t        let body_start = buf.pos;\n263\t        let body_len = sec_len - 5;\n264\t        let sec_body = &msg[body_start..body_start + body_len];\n265\t\n266\t        match sec_num {\n267\t            1 => {\n268\t                let (center, subcenter, ref_time) = parse_section1(sec_body)?;\n269\t                builder.center = Some(center);\n270\t                builder.subcenter = Some(subcenter);\n271\t                builder.ref_time = Some(ref_time);\n272\t            }\n273\t            2 => { /* Local Use section — skip */ }\n274\t            3 => {\n275\t                let (gdt, grid) = parse_section3(sec_body)?;\n276\t                builder.gdt_template = Some(gdt);\n277\t                builder.grid = Some(grid);\n278\t            }\n279\t            4 => {\n280\t                let (pdt, param, fore, lvl, ens) = parse_section4(sec_body, discipline)?;\n281\t                builder.pdt_template = Some(pdt);\n282\t                builder.parameter = Some(param);\n283\t                builder.forecast = Some(fore);\n284\t                builder.level = Some(lvl);\n285\t                builder.ensemble = Some(ens);\n286\t            }\n287\t            5 => {\n288\t                let (drt, packing, complex_extra, n_packed) = parse_section5(sec_body)?;\n289\t                builder.drt_template = Some(drt);\n290\t                builder.packing = Some(packing);\n291\t                builder.complex_extra = complex_extra;\n292\t                builder.n_packed = Some(n_packed);\n293\t            }\n294\t            6 => {\n295\t                let (has_bitmap, bitmap) = parse_section6(sec_body)?;\n296\t                builder.has_bitmap = Some(has_bitmap);\n297\t                builder.bitmap = bitmap;\n298\t            }\n299\t            7 => {\n300\t                let n_grid = builder.grid.as_ref().map(|g| g.num_data_points as usize).unwrap_or(0);\n301\t                let has_bitmap = builder.has_bitmap.unwrap_or(false);\n302\t                // When a bitmap is present, Section 5 n_packed < n_grid. Use n_packed\n303\t                // for the data unpackers (which only see the \"present\" subset).\n304\t                let n_decode = if has_bitmap {\n305\t                    builder.n_packed.unwrap_or(n_grid)\n306\t                } else {\n307\t                    n_grid\n308\t                };\n309\t                let packing = builder.packing.as_ref().ok_or(Error::NotImplemented)?;\n310\t                let drt = builder.drt_template.unwrap_or(0);\n311\t                let packed_values = decode_section7(\n312\t                    sec_body, packing, drt, builder.complex_extra.as_ref(), n_decode,\n313\t                )?;\n314\t                // Expand packed values into the full grid using the bitmap (if present).\n315\t                let values = if has_bitmap {\n316\t                    expand_bitmap(packed_values, &builder.bitmap, n_grid)\n317\t                } else {\n318\t builder.grid.clone();\n324\t                let prev_gdt_template = builder.gdt_template;\n325\t                let next_builder = FieldBuilder {\n326\t                    center: builder.center,\n327\t                    subcenter: builder.subcenter,\n328\t                    ref_time: builder.ref_time,\n329\t                    // Preserve grid definition for subsequent fields in multi-field messages\n330\t                    grid: prev_grid,\n331\t                    gdt_template: prev_gdt_template,\n332\t                    ..Default::default()\n333\t                };\n334\t                if let Some(field) = builder.build() {\n335\t                    out.push(field);\n336\t                }\n337\t                builder = next_builder;\n338\t            }\n339\t            _ => { /* Unknown section — skip */ }\n340\t        }\n341\t\n342\t        // Advance buf.pos to the end of this section.\n343\t        buf.pos = sec_start + sec_len;\n344\t    }\n345\t\n346\t    // Consume \"7777\" end marker.\n347\t    let end = &msg[body_end..body_end + 4];\n348\t    if end != b\"7777\" {\n349\t        return Err(Error::TooShort { needed: 4, got: 0 });\n350\t    }\n351\t\n352\t    Ok(total_len)\n353\t}\n354\t\n355\t// ── Section 1: Identification ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n356\t\n357\tfn parse_section1(body: &[u8]) -> Result<(u16, u16, ReferenceTime)> {\n358\t    let mut b = Buf::new(body);\n359\t    // oct 6-7 of section (indices 0-1 in body): originating center\n360\t    let center = b.read_u16be()?;\n361\t    //    let second = b.read_u8()?;\n372\t    // production status and type of data — not stored in Field currently\n373\t    Ok((\n374\t        center,\n375\t        subcenter,\n376\t        ReferenceTime { year, month, day, hour, minute, second, significance },\n377\t    ))\n378\t}\n379\t\n380\t// ── Section 3: Grid Definition ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n381\t\n382\tfn                            // oct 68–71 (N, not Dj)\n640\t    let scanning_mode = b.read_u8()?;     // oct 72\n641\t\n642\t    let projection = GridProjection::GaussianLatLon(GaussianLatLonParams { n_parallels });\n643\t\n644\t    Ok(GridDefinition {\n645\t        template: 40,\n646\t        num_data_points,\n647\t        nx,\n648\t        ny,\n649\t        lat_first,\n650\t        lon_first,\n651\t        lat_last,\n652\t        lon_last,\n653\t        di,\n654\t        dj: 0.0,   // not stored in GDT 3.40; N replaces Dj\n655\t        scanning_mode,\n656\t        resolution_flags,\n657\t        shape_of_earth,\n658\t        projection,\n659\t    })\n660\t}\n661\t\n662\t// ── Section 4: Product Definition ────────────────────────────────────────────\n663\t\n664\tfn parse_section4(\n665\t    body: &[u8],\n666\t    discipline: u8,\n667\t) -> Result<(u16, ParameterId, ForecastTime, Level, Option<Ensemble>)> {\n668\t    let mut b = Buf::new(body);\n669\t    let _n_coord = b.read_u16be()?; // oct 6-7: number of coordinate values\n670\t    let template = b.read_u16be()?; // oct 8-9: PDT template number\n671\t\n672\t    match template {\n673\t        0 => {\n674\t            let (param, fore, lvl, ens) = parse_pdt_0(&mut b, discipline)?;\n675\t            Ok((0, param, fore, lvl, ens))\n676\t        }\n677\t        1 => {\n678\t            let (param, fore, lvl, ens) = parse_pdt_1(&mut b, discipline)?;\n679\t            Ok((1, param, fore, lvl, ens))\n680\t        }\n681\t        8 => {\n682\t            let (param, fore, lvl, ens) = parse_pdt_8(&mut b, discipline)?;\n683\t            Ok((8, param, fore, lvl, ens))\n684\t        }\n685\t        11 => {\n686\t            let (param, fore, lvl, ens) = parse_pdt_11(&mut b, discipline)?;\n687\t            Ok((11, param, fore, lvl, ens))\n688\t        }\n689\t        _ => Err(Error::NotImplemented),\n690\t    }\n691\t}\n692\t\n693\t/// Parse the common PDT header fields shared by templates 4.0, 4.1, 4.8, 4.11.\n694\t///\n695\t/// Reads octets 10–34 (parameter, time, and level fields).  The caller reads\n696\t/// any template-specific tail octets after calling this function.\n697\tfn parse_pdt_common_header(\n698\t    b: &mut Buf,\n699\t    discipline: u8,\n700\t) -> Result<(ParameterId, ForecastTime, Level)> {\n701\t    let category = b.read_u8()?;  // oct 10\n702\t    let number = b.read_u8()?;    // oct 11\n703\t    b.skip(1)?; // generating process type (oct 12)\n704\t    b.skip(1)?; // background generating process id (oct 13)\n705\t    b.skip(1)?; // analysis/forecast generating process id (oct 14)\n706\t    b.skip(2)?; // hours of cutoff after reference time (oct 15-16)\n707\t    b.skip(1)?; // minutes of cutoff (oct 17)\n708\t    let time_range_unit = b.read_u8()?;    // oct 18\n709\t    let forecast_offset = b.read_u32be()?; // oct 19-22\n710\t\n711\t    let type1 = b.read_u8()?;                     // oct 23\n712\t    let scale_factor1 = b.read_i8()?;             // oct 24\n713\t    let scaled_value1 = b.read_u32be()? as i32;   // oct 25-28\n714\t\n715\t    let raw_type2 = b.read_u8()?;                     // oct 29\n716\t    let raw_scale_factor2 = b.read_i8()?;             // oct 30\n717\t    let raw_scaled_value2 = b.read_u32be()? as i32;   // oct 31-34\n718\t\n719\t    // When second surface type is 255 (missing), zero out its scale/value\n720\t    // to match eccodes behavior.\n721\t    let (type2, scale_factor2, scaled_value2) = if raw_type2 == 255 {\n722\t        (255u8, 0i8, 0i32)\n723\t    } else {\n724\t        (raw_type2, raw_scale_factor2, raw_scaled_value2)\n725\t    };\n726\t\n727\t    let param = ParameterId { discipline, category, number };\n728\t    // Reference time is filled in from Section 1 by the caller.\n729\t    let fore = ForecastTime {\n730\t        reference_time: ReferenceTime {\n731\t            year: 0, month: 0, day: 0, hour: 0, minute: 0, second: 0, significance: 0,\n732\t        },\n733\t        time_range_unit,\n734\t        forecast_offset,\n735\t    };\n736\t    let lvl = Level { type1, scale_factor1, scaled_value1, type2, scale_factor2, scaled_value2 };\n737\t\n738\t    Ok((param, fore, lvl))\n739\t}\n740\t\n741\t/// Product Definition Template 4.0: Analysis or forecast at horizontal level.\n742\tfn parse_pdt_0(\n743\t    b: &mut Buf,\n744\t    discipline: u8,\n745\t) -> Result<(ParameterId, ForecastTime, Level, Option<Ensemble>)> {\n746\t    let (param, fore, lvl) = parse_pdt_common_header(b, discipline)?;\n747\t    Ok((param, fore, lvl, None))\n748\t}\n749\t\n750\t/// Product Definition Template 4.1: Individual ensemble forecast, control and\n751\t/// perturbed, at a horizontal level at a point in time.\n752\t///\n753\t/// WMO GRIB2 Table 4.1:\n754\t/// - Octs 10–34: common header (same as PDT 4.0)\n755\t/// - Oct 35: type of ensemble forecast (Table 4.6)\n756\t/// - Oct 36: perturbation number\n757\t/// - Oct 37: number of forecasts in ensemble\n758\tfn parse_pdt_1(\n759\t    b: &mut Buf,\n760\t    discipline: u8,\n761\t) -> Result<(ParameterId, ForecastTime, Level, Option<Ensemble>)> {\n762\t    let (param, fore, lvl) = parse_pdt_common_header(b, discipline)?;\n763\t\n764\t    let member_type = b.read_u8()?;          // oct 35: Table 4.6\n765\t    let perturbation_number = b.read_u8()?;  // oct 36\n766\t    let _n_ensemble = b.read_u8()?;          // oct 37: number in ensemble (unused by harness)\n767\t\n768\t    let ens = Ensemble { member_type, number: perturbation_number as i16 };\n769\t    Ok((param, fore, lvl, Some(ens)))\n770\t}\n771\t\n772\t/// Product Definition Template 4.8: Average, accumulation, extreme values or\n773\t/// other statistically-processed values at a horizontal level in a continuous\n774\t/// or non-continuous time interval.\n775\t///\n776\t/// WMO GRIB2 Table 4.8:\n777\t/// - Octs 10–34: common header (same as PDT 4.0)\n778\t/// - Oct 35: year (u16), month, day, hour, minute, second of end of interval\n779\t/// - Oct 41: number of time range specifications (n)\n780\t/// - Octs 42 onward: n × 12-byte time range specifications (skipped)\n781\t///\n782\t/// Only the common header fields are surfaced; the statistical window\n783\t/// information is not yet modelled in `ForecastTime`.\n784\tfn parse_pdt_8(\n785\t    b: &mut Buf,\n786\t    discipline: u8,\n787\t) -> Result<(ParameterId, ForecastTime, Level, Option<Ensemble>)> {\n788\t    let (param, fore, lvl) = parse_pdt_common_header(b, discipline)?;\n789\t\n790\t    // End-of-interval timestamp and time-range specs: skip entirely.\n791\t    // Oct 35-40: end time (year u16 + month + day + hour + min + sec = 7 bytes)\n792\t    b.skip(7)?;\n793\t    // Oct 41: number of time range specs\n794\t    let n_ranges = b.read_u8()? as usize;\n795\t    // Each spec is 12 bytes.\n796\t    b.skip(12 * n_ranges)?;\n797\t\n798\t    Ok((param, fore, lvl, None))\n799\t}\n800\t\n801\t/// Product Definition Template 4.11: Individual ensemble member +\n802\t/// time-processed statistical product at a horizontal level.\n803\t///\n804\t/// WMO GRIB2 Table 4.11:\n805\t/// - Octs 10–34: common header (same as PDT 4.0)\n806\t/// - Oct 35: type of ensemble forecast (Table 4.6)\n807\t/// - Oct 36: perturbation number\n808\t/// - Oct 37: number of forecasts in ensemble\n809\t/// - Oct 38-43: end-of-interval timestamp (year u16 + month + day + hour + min + sec)\n810\t/// - Oct 44: number of time range specifications (n)\n811\t/// - Octs 45+: n × 12-byte time range specs (skipped)\n812\tfn parse_pdt_11(\n813\t    b: &mut Buf,\n814\t    discipline: u8,\n815\t) -> Result<(ParameterId, ForecastTime, Level, Option<Ensemble>)> {\n816\t    let (param, fore, lvl) = parse_pdt_common_header(b, discipline)?;\n817\t\n818\t    let member_type = b.read_u8()?;          // oct 35\n819\t    let perturbation_number = b.read_u8()?;  // oct 36\n820\t    let _n_ensemble = b.read_u8()?;          // oct 37\n821\t\n822\t    // Oct 38-43: end-of-interval timestamp (7 bytes: year u16 + month + day + hour + min + sec)\n823\t    b.skip(7)?;\n824\t    // Oct 44: number of time range specs\n825\t    let n_ranges = b.read_u8()? as usize;\n826\t    b.skip(12 * n_ranges)?;\n827\t\n828\t    let ens = Ensemble { member_type, number: perturbation_number as i16 };\n829\t    Ok((param, fore, lvl, Some(ens)))\n830\t}\n831\t\n832\t// ── Section 5: Data Representation ───────────────────────────────────────────\n833\t\n834\tfn parse_section5(body: &[u8]) -> Result<(u16, PackingInfo, Option<ComplexPackingExtra>, usize)> {\n835\t    let mut b = Buf::new(body);\n836\t    let n_values = b.read_u32be()? as usize; // oct 6-9: number of packed values\n837\t    let template = b.read_u16be()?;           // oct 10-11: DRT template number\n838\t\n839\t    match template {\n840\t        0 => {\n841\t            let packing = parse_drt_common(&mut b)?;\n842\t            Ok((0, packing, None, n_values))\n843\t        }\n844\t        2 => {\n845\t            let (packing, extra) = parse_drt_2(&mut b)?;\n846\t            Ok((2, packing, Some(extra), n_values))\n847\t        }\n848\t        3 => {\n849\t            let (packing, extra) = parse_drt_3(&mut b)?;\n850\t            Ok((3, packing, Some(extra), n_values))\n851\t        }\n852\t        40 => {\n853\t            // Template 5.40: JPEG 2000 data compression — same common header as DRT=0.\n854\t            let packing = parse_drt_common(&mut b)?;\n855\t            Ok((40, packing, None, n_values))\n856\t        }\n857\t        41 => {\n858\t            // Template 5.41: PNG data compression — same common header as DRT=0.\n859\t            let packing = parse_drt_common(&mut b)?;\n860\t            Ok((41, packing, None, n_values))\n861\t        }\n862\t        _ => Err(Error::NotImplemented),\n863\t    }\n864\t}\n865\t\n866\t/// Parse the common packing header shared by DRT templates 0, 2, and 3.\n867\tfn parse_drt_common(b: &mut Buf) -> Result<PackingInfo> {\n868\t    let reference_value = b.read_f32be()?;               // oct 12-15: R\n869\t    let binary_scale_factor = b.read_scale_factor_i16()?; // oct 16-17: E\n870\t    let decimal_scale_factor = b.read_scale_factor_i16()?; // oct 18-19: D\n871\t    let bits_per_value = b.read_u8()?;                   // oct 20: N\n872\t    let original_field_type = b.read_u8()?;              // oct 21\n873\t\n874\t    Ok(PackingInfo {\n875\t        reference_value,\n876\t        binary_scale_factor,\n877\t        decimal_scale_factor,\n878\t        bits_per_value,\n879\t        original_field_type,\n880\t    })\n881\t}\n882\t\n883\t/// Data Representation Template 5.2: Complex packing (no spatial differencing).\n884\tfn parse_drt_2(b: &mut Buf) -> Result<(PackingInfo, ComplexPackingExtra)> {\n885\t    let packing = parse_drt_common(b)?;  // oct 12-21: common header\n886\t\n887\t    b.skip(1)?; // oct 22: group splitting method\n888\t    b.skip(1)?; // oct 23: missing value management (0 = none)\n889\t    b.skip(4)?; // oct 24-27: primary missing value\n890\t    b.skip(4)?; // oct 28-31: secondary missing value\n891\t\n892\t    let n_groups = b.read_u32be()?;              // oct 32-35\n893\t    let ref_group_widths = b.read_u8()?;         // oct 36\n894\t    let bits_group_widths = b.read_u8()?;        // oct 37\n895\t    let ref_group_lengths = b.read_u32be()?;     // oct 38-41\n896\t    let length_increment = b.read_u8()?;         // oct 42\n897\t    let true_last_group_length = b.read_u32be()?; // oct 43-46\n898\t    let bits_scaled_group_lengths = b.read_u8()?; // oct 47\n899\t    // Octets 48-49 (order_spatial_diff, extra_octet_count) are absent in template 5.2.\n900\t\n901\t    Ok((packing, ComplexPackingExtra {\n902\t        n_groups,\n903\t        ref_group_widths,\n904\t        bits_group_widths,\n905\t        ref_group_lengths,\n906\t        length_increment,\n907\t        true_last_group_length,\n908\t        bits_scaled_group_lengths,\n909\t        order_spatial_diff: 0,\n910\t        extra_octet_count: 0,\n911\t    }))\n912\t}\n913\t\n914\t/// Data Representation Template 5.3: Complex packing with spatial differencing.\n915\tfn parse_drt_3(b: &mut Buf) -> Result<(PackingInfo, ComplexPackingExtra)> {\n916\t    let packing = parse_drt_common(b)?;  // oct 12-21: common header\n917\t\n918\t    b.skip(1)?; // oct 22: group splitting method\n919\t    b.skip(1)?; // oct 23: missing value management (0 = none)\n920\t    b.skip(4)?; // oct 24-27: primary missing value\n921\t    b.skip(4)?; // oct 28-31: secondary missing value\n922\t\n923\t    let n_groups = b.read_u32be()?;              // oct 32-35\n924\t    let ref_group_widths = b.read_u8()?;         // oct 36\n925\t    let bits_group_widths = b.read_u8()?;        // oct 37\n926\t    let ref_group_lengths = b.read_u32be()?;     // oct 38-41\n927\t    let length_increment = b.read_u8()?;         // oct 42\n928\t    let true_last_group_length = b.read_u32be()?; // oct 43-46\n929\t    let bits_scaled_group_lengths = b.read_u8()?; // oct 47\n930\t    let order_spatial_diff = b.read_u8()?;       // oct 48\n931\t    let extra_octet_count = b.read_u8()?;        // oct 49\n932\t\n933\t    Ok((packing, ComplexPackingExtra {\n934\t        n_groups,\n935\t        ref_group_widths,\n936\t        bits_group_widths,\n937\t        ref_group_lengths,\n938\t        length_increment,\n939\t        true_last_group_length,\n940\t        bits_scaled_group_lengths,\n941\t        order_spatial_diff,\n942\t        extra_octet_count,\n943\t    }))\n944\t}\n945\t\n946\t// ── Section 6: Bit Map ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n947\t\n948\t/// Parse Section 6 (Bit Map).\n949\t///\n950\t/// Returns `(has_bitmap, bitmap_bytes)`:\n951\t/// - `has_bitmap=false, bitmap_bytes=None` when indicator == 255 (all points present).\n952\t/// - `has_bitmap=true, bitmap_bytes=Some(bytes)` when indicator == 0: one bit per grid\n953\t///   point, MSB-first packed, length = ceil(n_grid_points / 8).\n954\tfn parse_section6(body: &[u8]) -> Result<(bool, Option<Vec<u8>>)> {\n955\t    let mut b = Buf::new(body);\n956\t    let indicator = b.read_u8()?; // oct 6\n957\t    match indicator {\n958\t        255 => Ok((false, None)),\n959\t        0 => {\n960\t            // Remaining bytes are the bitmap (1 bit per grid point, MSB first).\n961\t            let bitmap = body[1..].to_vec();\n962\t            Ok((true, Some(bitmap)))\n963\t        }\n964\t        _ => Err(Error::NotImplemented),\n965\t    }\n966\t}\n967\t\n968\t// ── Bitmap expansion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n969\t\n970\t/// Expand a vector of packed (present-only) values into a full `n_grid`-length\n971\t/// masked grid using the bitmap.\n972\t///\n973\t/// The bitmap is a packed MSB-first bit array (one bit per grid point). Where\n974\t/// the bit is 1, the next value from `packed` is used; where 0, the grid point\n975\t/// is absent (value = 0.0, present = false). Returns `GridValues::Masked` if\n976\t/// a bitmap is provided and `n_packed < n_grid`, otherwise returns the input\n977\t/// as a `Dense` grid.\n978\tfn expand_bitmap(\n979\t    packed: GridValues,\n980\t    bitmap: &Option<Vec<u8>>,\n981\t    n_grid: usize,\n982\t) -> GridValues {\n983\t    let bm = match bitmap {\n984\t        Some(bm) => bm,\n985\t        None => return packed, // no bitmap — pass through\n986\t    };\n987\t\n988\t    let packed_vals = match packed {\n989\t        GridValues::Dense(v) => v,\n990\t        other => return other, // already masked somehow — pass through\n991\t    };\n992\t\n993\t    if packed_vals.len() == n_grid {\n994\t        // The packed count already matches the grid — no expansion needed.\n995\t        return GridValues::Dense(packed_vals);\n996\t    }\n997\t\n998\t    let mut values = vec![0.0f64; n_grid];\n999\t    let mut present = vec![false; n_grid];\n1000\t    let mut packed_idx = 0usize;\n1001\t\n1002\t    for grid_idx in 0..n_grid {\n1003\t        let byte = grid_idx / 8;\n1004\t        let bit = 7 - (grid_idx % 8); // MSB first\n1005\t        let is_present = byte < bm.len() && (bm[byte] >> bit) & 1 == 1;\n1006\t        if is_present {\n1007\t            if packed_idx < packed_vals.len() {\n1008\t                values[grid_idx] = packed_vals[packed_idx];\n1009\t                packed_idx += 1;\n1010\t            }\n1011\t            present[grid_idx] = true;\n1012\t        }\n1013\t    }\n1014\t\n1015\t    GridValues::Masked { values, present }\n1016\t}\n1017\t\n1018\t// ── Section 7: Data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1019\t\n1020\tfn decode_section7(\n1021\t    body: &[u8],\n1022\t    packing: &PackingInfo,\n1023\t    drt: u16,\n1024\t    complex_extra: Option<&ComplexPackingExtra>,\n1025\t    n_points: usize,\n1026\t) -> Result<GridValues> {\n1027\t    if let Some(extra) = complex_extra {\n1028\t        return decode_drt3(body, packing, extra, n_points);\n1029\t    }\n1030\t\n1031\t    if drt == 40 {\n1032\t        #[cfg(feature = \"jpeg2000\")]\n1033\t        return decode_drt40(body, packing, n_points);\n1034\t        #[cfg(not(feature = \"jpeg2000\"))]\n1035\t        return Err(Error::NotImplemented);\n1036\t    }\n1037\t\n1038\t    if drt == 41 {\n1039\t        return decode_drt41(body, packing, n_points);\n1040\t    }\n1041\t\n1042\t    // DRT=0: simple packing.\n1043\t    let r = packing.reference_value as f64;\n1044\t    let e = packing.binary_scale_factor as i32;\n1045\t    let d = packing.decimal_scale_factor as i32;\n1046\t    let two_e = 2f64.powi(e);\n1047\t    let ten_d = 10f64.powi(d);\n1048\t\n1049\t    match packing.bits_per_value {\n1050\t        0 => {\n1051\t            // Constant field: X=0 for all points, so Y = (R + 0) / 10^D = R / 10^D.\n1052\t            let v = r / ten_d;\n1053\t            Ok(GridValues::Dense(vec![v; n_points]))\n1054\t        }\n1055\t        n_bits => {\n1056\t            let packed = unpack_n_bits(body, n_points, n_bits as usize);\n1057\t            // WMO spec: Y × 10^D = R + X × 2^E  →  Y = (R + X × 2^E) / 10^D\n1058\t            let values: Vec<f64> = packed.iter().map(|&x| (r + x as f64 * two_e) / ten_d).collect();\n1059\t            Ok(GridValues::Dense(values))\n1060\t        }\n1061\t    }\n1062\t}\n1063\t\n1064\t/// Decode Template 5.40: JPEG 2000 data compression.\n1065\t///\n1066\t/// Section 7 contains a JPEG 2000 codestream (J2K) or JP2 container. The first\n1067\t/// component carries packed integers X; decoded values follow: Y = (R + X × 2^E) / 10^D.\n1068\t#[cfg(feature = \"jpeg2000\")]\n1069\tfn decode_drt40(body: &[u8], packing: &PackingInfo, n_points: usize) -> Result<GridValues> {\n1070\t    let img = jpeg2k::Image::from_bytes(body)\n1071\t        .map_err(|_| Error::InvalidData(\"JPEG2000 decode failed\"))?;\n1072\t    let comp = img.components().first()\n1073\t        .ok_or(Error::InvalidData(\"J2K: no image components\"))?;\n1074\t\n1075\t    let r = packing.reference_value as f64;\n1076\t    let e = packing.binary_scale_factor as i32;\n1077\t    let d = packing.decimal_scale_factor as i32;\n1078\t    let two_e = 2f64.powi(e);\n1079\t    let ten_d = 10f64.powi(d);\n1080\t\n1081\t    let data = comp.data(); // &[i32] — raw packed integer X values\n1082\t    let values: Vec<f64> = data.iter()\n1083\t        .take(n_points)\n1084\t        .map(|&x| (r + x as f64 * two_e) / ten_d)\n1085\t        .collect();\n1086\t\n1087\t    if values.len() < n_points {\n1088\t        return Err(Error::InvalidData(\"J2K: fewer pixels than grid points\"));\n1089\t    }\n1090\t\n1091\t    Ok(GridValues::Dense(values))\n1092\t}\n1093\t\n1094\t/// Decode Template 5.41: PNG data compression.\n1095\t///\n1096\t/// Section 7 contains a raw PNG image. Pixel values are packed integers X;\n1097\t/// decoded grid values follow the standard formula: Y = (R + X × 2^E) / 10^D.\n1098\t/// Only 8-bit and 16-bit grayscale PNGs are supported (the common GRIB2 case).\n1099\tfn decode_drt41(body: &[u8], packing: &PackingInfo, n_points: usize) -> Result<GridValues> {\n1100\t    let cursor = std::io::Cursor::new(body);\n1101\t    let decoder = png::Decoder::new(cursor);\n1102\t    let mut reader = decoder.read_info().map_err(|_| Error::InvalidData(\"PNG header decode failed\"))?;\n1103\t\n1104\t    let buf_size = reader.output_buffer_size().ok_or(Error::InvalidData(\"PNG: buffer size unknown\"))?;\n1105\t    let mut img_data = vec![0u8; The key savings vs. the\n1304\t/// per-element path:\n1305\t///\n1306\t/// * No `div_ceil` per element — `bytes_needed` is computed once on pre-fill.\n1307\t/// * No inner byte-assembly loop per element — bytes are amortised over a\n1308\t///   window: one byte loaded per 8 bits consumed on average.\n1309\t/// * Single `shift + mask` per value instead of 3–9 byte-load + shift operations.\n1310\t///\n1311\t/// The left-aligned invariant: valid bits always occupy the MSB positions of\n1312\t/// `buf`, so the next `w`-bit value is always extracted as `(buf >> (64 - w)) & mask`.\n1313\t///\n1314\t/// # Panics (debug only)\n1315\t/// `w` must satisfy `0 < w ≤ 32`. from `data` starting at `bit_offset` (MSB-first).\n1382\tfn read_bits_at(data: &[u8], bit_offset: usize, n_bits: usize) -> u64 {\n1383\t    if n_bits == 0 {\n1384\t        return 0;\n1385\t mask\n1399\t}\n1400\t\n1401\t/// Extract `count` unsigned integers each `n_bits` wide from `data`.\n1402\t/// Bits are packed MSB-first: the first value occupies bits [0..n_bits-1]\n1403\t/// of the
